topic: ThreadRAII Design: Accessing the Underlying Thread Object
explanation: When creating RAII wrappers (like `ThreadRAII`) around `std::thread` to enforce cleanup (joining/detaching), it is often necessary to expose the underlying `std::thread` object. This is typically done via a `get()` member function, analogous to the `get()` functions provided by standard smart pointers (`std::unique_ptr`, `std::shared_ptr`). This approach avoids forcing the wrapper class to replicate the entire interface of `std::thread` and allows the RAII object to be used in contexts where a raw `std::thread` object is required.
practical_example: A developer needs to wrap thread management but occasionally must call a specialized third-party function that accepts a `std::thread&`. The `get()` function allows the wrapper to fulfill this requirement without breaking encapsulation of the RAII cleanup logic.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
